correctness.rationale: Walsh E_j decompose into 1 radial vector w_j and unaffected dark projector F_j. Rank-one secular polynomial at lambda_j=d-2j equals -tau*m_j/N times nonzero product; bright Jacobi spectrum is simple and disjoint for tau!=0. PSD Schur squares yield f^T(F_j∘F_j)f=||F_j diag(f)F_j||_F^2; induction on Fourier even weight forces all even coefficients equal, so dark kernel=odd-Walsh⊕span(h), rank=N/2-1. Odd powers H^(2r+1) have diagonals zero for shell k>r and tau(r!)^2 at k=r. Bipartite symmetry cancels dark diagonal contributions; these odd moments span radial bright intensities of dimension d+1. Their overlap with the dark range has dimension floor(d/2), giving rank N/2+ceil(d/2) and kernel O∩R_perp. Separately tensorizing the unmarked probability matrix gives rank N/2 for tau=0. Independent eigensolver checks for d=1..4 and tau=-2,0,1.3 give the predicted ranks; these are not a proof for all d.
